mainTopic: End of פרק סדר תעניות אלו (הלל after rain), then the משנה of פרק בשלשה פרקים: ברכת כהנים, the מעמדות, the wood-offering dates, and the start of the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז and תשעה באב
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous sugya. If rain falls during a fast, people eat first and only then say הלל, since הלל is said on a full stomach. The גמרא challenges this from רב פפא, who had people say הלל before eating. It answers that the people of מחוזא were an exception because they tended to get drunk. The פרק then closes with a הדרן, and a new פרק opens with a משנה. That משנה lists three occasions when כהנים say ברכת כהנים four times in one day: fast days, מעמדות, and יום כיפור. It explains the מעמדות: groups of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים who stood in for the whole nation at the daily קרבן. It also describes their fasts, their daily readings of מעשה בראשית, and which of their gatherings were cancelled on days with הלל, מוסף, or a קרבן עצים, a point on which רבי עקיבא accepted בן עזאי's version. The משנה lists the nine dates when families brought wood for the מזבח, and then begins a new section on the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז and תשעה באב, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: הלל is said only on a full stomach
steps.stepSummary: The end of the previous ruling: after rain ends a fast, people should eat first, because הלל is said only when one is full and satisfied.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We do not say הלל] except on a satisfied soul and a full stomach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that started on the previous amud. If rain falls during a fast, people go home, eat and drink, and only then say הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is that הלל is a song of joy. It should be said with a satisfied, happy feeling, not while still hungry from fasting. This ruling is the target of the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A satisfied soul (feeling full and content)
A full stomach
Psalms of praise said on joyful occasions

phrases.english: except on a satisfied soul
phrases.notes: Continues a sentence from the previous amud: 'We do not say הלל...'

phrases.english: and a full stomach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עַל נֶפֶשׁ שְׂבֵעָה וְכָרֵס מְלֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a statement begun on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל after rain on a fast day is said only after eating, on a full stomach.

steps.title: Challenge from רב פפא saying הלל before eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule with a story. רב פפא decreed a fast in a shul, rain fell before midday, and he had them say הלל first and eat afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב פפא came to the shul of אבי גובר and decreed a fast. Rain fell for them before midday, and he told them: Say הלל, and afterward eat and drink!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from Step 1 by bringing a real story that seems to show the opposite practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said to eat first and say הלל afterward. רב פפא did the reverse: הלל first, food afterward. So either the rule is wrong, or something about this case was special.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (opens a challenge)
But behold (introduces a contradicting source)
Happened to come / visited
Decreed a fast
Before midday

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Rav Pappa happened to come
to the synagogue of Avi Govar
and decreed a fast,
and rain fell for them before midday,
and he said [to them: Say] Hallel
and afterward eat and drink!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַב פָּפָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא דַּאֲבִי גוֹבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that הלל is said only after eating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A practical story shows a great אמורא having people say הלל before eating, which contradicts the rule.

steps.title: The people of מחוזא were different
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the people of מחוזא tended to get drunk. If רב פפא had sent them to eat and drink first, they would not have been fit to say הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of מחוזא are different, because drunkenness is common among them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule. רב פפא's case was a special exception because of the people he was dealing with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule stays the same: eat first, then say הלל. In מחוזא, people would likely drink too much and be unable to pray properly. So רב פפא reversed the order for them only.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different (signals an exception)
מחוזא, a wealthy Babylonian city
Drunkenness

steps.whatToRemember: The ideal is to eat first and then say הלל with joy. Where people are likely to get drunk, הלל is said first.

phrases.english: The people of Mechoza are different,
for drunkenness is common among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי בְּנֵי מָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's practice shows that הלל always comes before eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stands. מחוזא was an exception because of the risk of drunkenness.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter סדר תעניות אלו
steps.stepSummary: This is the formal closing line of the third פרק of מסכת תענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, סדר תעניות אלו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a formula that marks the end of the פרק. It is not an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learners traditionally say הדרן to show their attachment to the material and their hope to learn it again. Everything after this line belongs to a new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (end-of-chapter formula)
Name of the third פרק of תענית

phrases.english: We will return to you, Seder Taaniyot Elu

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ סֵדֶר תַּעֲנִיּוֹת אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The third פרק of תענית ends here.

steps.title: Three occasions with four rounds of the priestly blessing
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that on three occasions, כהנים do נשיאת כפים four times in one day: at שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה. The occasions are fast days, מעמדות, and יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: At three times in the year, כהנים raise their hands four times in the day: at שחרית, at מוסף, at מנחה, and at נעילת שערים. These are on fast days, on מעמדות, and on יום כיפור.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It states a rule about which days have four rounds of ברכת כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually ברכת כהנים is said at most twice a day: at שחרית, and at מוסף on days that have מוסף. On these three occasions it is also said at מנחה and at נעילה, so כהנים bless four times. Not every occasion actually has all four prayers, and the גמרא will discuss this later. For now, just learn the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Times / occasions (here, not 'chapters')
Raise their hands, i.e., say ברכת כהנים
Closing of the gates, the נעילה prayer
Groups of Jews who stood by the daily offerings to represent everyone

steps.confusionAlert: Here פרקים means 'times of the year,' not 'chapters.' Also, do not mix up the two lists. The four items (שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, נעילה) are four prayers. The three occasions are fast days, מעמדות, and יום כיפור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the foundation for the whole פרק. The גמרא will ask which of these days really have מוסף and נעילה, and how ברכת כהנים relates to fasting.

phrases.english: At three times in the year
priests raise their hands
four times in the day;
at the morning prayer, the additional prayer, the afternoon prayer,
and at the closing of the gates:
on fast days, and on the non-priestly watches,
and on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים בְּשָׁנָה כֹּהֲנִים נוֹשְׂאִין אֶת כַּפֵּיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On fast days, מעמדות, and יום כיפור, כהנים say ברכת כהנים four times: at שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה.

steps.title: The verse behind the מעמדות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts explaining what מעמדות are. It quotes the פסוק that calls the daily offering 'My offering, My food' and is addressed to all of בני ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the מעמדות: since it says, 'Command the children of Israel: My offering, My food...'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins defining מעמדות, which it mentioned in Step 5, by quoting a פסוק. This is a setup for the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks to all of בני ישראל about the קרבן תמיד. This shows that the daily offering belongs to the whole nation, not only to the כהנים. That idea leads to the problem raised next.

keyTerms.meaning: These are (introduces a definition)
Since it is stated (introduces a פסוק)
My offering, My food (the daily תמיד)

phrases.english: These are the non-priestly watches.
Since it is stated:
"Command the children of Israel
My offering, My food"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ הֵן מַעֲמָדוֹת. לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a term mentioned in the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daily offering is the obligation of all of בני ישראל, as the פסוק is addressed to them.

steps.title: How can an offering be brought without its owner present?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks: if the קרבן belongs to every Jew, how can it be offered when the owners are not standing next to it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But how can a person's offering be sacrificed when he is not standing by it?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה raises a question that sets up its explanation of how the מעמדות were created. The answer comes in the next part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person should normally be present when his קרבן is offered. Since the תמיד belongs to the entire nation, it is impossible for everyone to be in ירושלים every day. That problem is what the מעמדות system will solve.

keyTerms.meaning: But how could it be? (introduces a question)
Is offered / sacrificed
Stands over it (is present by it)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הֵיאַךְ קׇרְבָּנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קָרֵב
phrases.english: But how can a person's offering be sacrificed
when he is not standing by it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הֵיאַךְ קׇרְבָּנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out a problem from the פסוק just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the whole nation can be present at its daily offering. This sets up the institution of the מעמדות.

steps.title: The prophets set up 24 watches, each with representatives
steps.stepSummary: The נביאים הראשונים divided the people into 24 משמרות. Each one had a מעמד in ירושלים made of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The early prophets set up twenty-four watches. For every single watch there was a standing group in Jerusalem, made of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question from step 7. Since all of כלל ישראל cannot stand by the קרבן, a set group of representatives stands there for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a person's קרבן normally needs its owner present, and every Jew owns the תמיד. The solution is representation. Each week one משמר serves, and its מעמד stands in the name of the whole nation. Including ישראלים, not only כהנים and לוים, is what lets the regular people count as present.

keyTerms.meaning: The early prophets (in the time of שמואל and דוד)
A priestly 'watch' or shift; there were 24, each serving one week at a time
A 'standing group' of representatives who stood by the קרבנות on behalf of all כלל ישראל
They instituted / set up

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the definition of a מעמד. Everything else here describes what these representatives did.

phrases.english: The early prophets instituted
twenty-four watches,
for each and every watch
there was a standing group in Jerusalem
phrases.notes: This group stood by the קרבן on behalf of everyone.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים שֶׁל לְוִיִּם וְשֶׁל יִשְׂרְאֵלִים.
phrases.english: of priests, of Levites, and of Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִינוּ נְבִיאִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה מִשְׁמָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question posed in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the communal קרבן be brought without its owners present?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through representation. Each of the 24 משמרות had a מעמד of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים who stood in for all of כלל ישראל.

steps.title: What happens when a watch's week arrives
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים and לוים go up to ירושלים. The ישראלים of that משמר who stay home gather in their towns and read מעשה בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it was time for the watch to go up, the כהנים and לוים went up to Jerusalem. The ישראלים of that watch gathered in their towns and read the story of Creation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the practical routine of a משמר's week. It explains what each group does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים and לוים go to serve in the בית המקדש. The ישראלים of that משמר who did not go up still take part from home: they gather and read about Creation. As the Sefaria note explains, some ישראלים went to ירושלים and the rest gathered at home.

keyTerms.meaning: They gather together
The account of Creation (בראשית chapter 1 to the start of chapter 2)
To go up (to ירושלים / to serve)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think every ישראל in the משמר stayed home. Some went up to ירושלים to stand by the קרבן. The ones described here are the rest, who gathered in their own towns.

phrases.english: When the time came for the watch to go up,
the priests and Levites go up to Jerusalem,
and the Israelites who belong to that watch
gather in their own towns,
and read the account of Creation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַמִּשְׁמָר לַעֲלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the מעמד to describing what its members actually do.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During their week, the כהנים and לוים serve in ירושלים, and the ישראלים of the משמר gather locally and read מעשה בראשית.

steps.title: The fasts of the standing group, Monday to Thursday
steps.stepSummary: The אנשי מעמד fasted four days, Monday to Thursday. They did not fast on Friday, out of honor for שבת. They did not fast on Sunday, so as not to jump straight from rest to hardship.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of the standing group fasted four days a week, from Monday to Thursday. They did not fast on Friday, out of respect for שבת. They did not fast on Sunday, so they would not go straight from rest and pleasure to effort and fasting and die.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another practice of the אנשי מעמד: weekly fasts. It gives a reason for skipping each end of the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate reasons are given. Friday is skipped for כבוד שבת: you should not enter שבת hungry and weak. Sunday is skipped for health: a sudden switch from שבת's rest and עונג to hard work plus fasting could be dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: The members of the standing group
They fast
Honor of שבת
Sunday (literally 'day one toward שבת')
Delight / pleasure

steps.confusionAlert: 'אחד בשבת' does not mean 'one on שבת'. It is the normal way the משנה says Sunday.

phrases.english: And the members of the standing group would fast
four days a week,
from Monday until Thursday.
And they would not fast on Friday —
out of honor for Shabbat,
and not on Sunday —
so that they should not go out from rest and delight
to exertion and fasting, and die.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַנְשֵׁי הַמַּעֲמָד הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים בַּשָּׁבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second practice of the אנשי מעמד, fasting, after the reading practice in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אנשי מעמד fast Monday through Thursday only. Friday is excluded because of כבוד שבת, and Sunday because of the danger of a sudden change.

steps.title: Which part of Creation is read on each day
steps.stepSummary: Each day of the week the אנשי מעמד read two sections of מעשה בראשית: that day's section plus the next one.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Sunday: 'In the beginning' and 'Let there be a firmament.' On Monday: 'Let there be a firmament' and 'Let the waters gather.' On Tuesday: 'Let the waters gather' and 'Let there be lights.' On Wednesday: 'Let there be lights' and 'Let the waters swarm.' On Thursday: 'Let the waters swarm' and 'Let the earth bring forth.' On Friday: 'Let the earth bring forth' and 'The heavens were finished.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now spells out the exact reading for each day, filling in the general statement from step 9 that they read מעשה בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a clear pattern: each day repeats the previous day's second section and adds the next one. So every day's reading overlaps with the day before. Each day's reading roughly matches what was created on that day of Creation.

keyTerms.meaning: Firmament / sky
'Let the waters gather'
Lights (sun, moon, stars)
'Let the waters swarm' (sea creatures)
'And they were finished' (start of בראשית chapter 2)

steps.confusionAlert: Although they fasted only Monday to Thursday, the reading happened on all six weekdays, including Sunday and Friday. Fasting and reading are separate practices.

phrases.english: On Sunday: 'In the beginning,' and 'Let there be a firmament.'
On Monday: 'Let there be a firmament,' and 'Let the waters gather.'
On Tuesday: 'Let the waters gather,' and 'Let there be lights.'
On Wednesday: 'Let there be lights,' and 'Let the waters swarm.'
On Thursday: 'Let the waters swarm,' and 'Let the earth bring forth.'
On Friday: 'Let the earth bring forth,' and 'The heavens were finished.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן: בְּרֵאשִׁית, וִיהִי רָקִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the details of the reading of מעשה בראשית mentioned in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each weekday the אנשי מעמד read that day's section of Creation together with the following section.

steps.title: How and when the daily reading was done
steps.stepSummary: A long section is read by two people and a short one by one person. At שחרית and מוסף they read from the ספר תורה. At מנחה they read by heart, like קריאת שמע. On Friday at מנחה they did not gather, out of honor for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A long section is read by two people, and a short section by one person. This is at שחרית and at מוסף. At מנחה they come in and read it by heart, the way people say שמע. On Friday at מנחה they did not come in, out of respect for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes describing the reading. It explains who reads, at which תפילות, and in what way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A long section (six or more פסוקים) is split between two readers. A short one is read by a single person, since each reader needs at least three פסוקים. In the morning they read from a ספר תורה. At מנחה they recite it from memory. On Friday afternoon even this is dropped, so people can prepare for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A long section (six or more פסוקים)
By one person alone
By heart / from memory
They enter (the בית הכנסת to gather)

steps.whatToRemember: A מעמד is a group of representatives who stand by the קרבן for all of כלל ישראל. The ישראלים among them who stayed home gathered in their towns. They fasted Monday to Thursday and read two sections of מעשה בראשית every weekday: from the ספר תורה at שחרית and מוסף, by heart at מנחה, and not at all at מנחה on Friday.

phrases.english: A long section is read by two people,
and the short one by a single person.
This is at the morning prayer and at the additional prayer.
And at the afternoon prayer they enter and read by heart,
just as people recite Shema.

phrases.aramaic: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּמִּנְחָה לֹא הָיוּ נִכְנָסִין —
phrases.english: On Friday at the afternoon prayer they would not enter —
out of honor for Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרָשָׁה גְּדוֹלָה קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ בִּשְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the readings listed in step 11 were carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A long section is split between two readers and a short one is read by one. They read from the ספר תורה at שחרית and מוסף, by heart at מנחה, and skip מנחה on Friday because of כבוד שבת.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's rule on which gatherings were canceled on special days
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rules: on a day with הלל there is no מעמד at שחרית; on a day with a קרבן מוסף there is none at נעילה; on a day with a קרבן עצים there is none at מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any day that has הלל: there is no מעמד at שחרית. A day with a קרבן מוסף: there is none at נעילה. A day with a קרבן עצים: there is none at מנחה. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new rule. On certain special days the אנשי מעמד did not hold one of their usual prayer gatherings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אנשי מעמד normally gathered for several prayers each day: שחרית, מוסף, מנחה and נעילה. Three kinds of special days each cancel one of these gatherings. Here, according to רבי עקיבא, הלל cancels שחרית, מוסף cancels נעילה, and wood cancels מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Praise psalms said on יום טוב, ראש חודש and חנוכה
The extra offering brought on שבת, יום טוב and ראש חודש
Wood donated for the מזבח by certain families on set dates
Morning prayer
Closing prayer at the end of the day
Afternoon prayer

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the whole day's מעמד is canceled. Each special day cancels one specific prayer gathering of the אנשי מעמד.

phrases.english: Any day that has Hallel —
there is no maamad at the morning prayer,
an additional offering — none at the closing prayer,
a wood offering — none at the afternoon prayer.
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הַלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the laws of the אנשי מעמד by naming days when one of their gatherings is canceled
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא: הלל cancels the שחרית gathering, מוסף cancels נעילה, and קרבן עצים cancels מנחה.

steps.title: בן עזאי reports רבי יהושע's different version
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי tells רבי עקיבא that רבי יהושע taught it differently: מוסף cancels מנחה, and קרבן עצים cancels נעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said to him: this is how רבי יהושע used to teach it. A day with a קרבן מוסף: there is no מעמד at מנחה. A day with a קרבן עצים: there is none at נעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי pushes back on רבי עקיבא. He quotes their teacher רבי יהושע, who had a different version of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for הלל stays the same. Only the last two items are switched. In רבי יהושע's version, מוסף cancels מנחה and wood cancels נעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: שמעון בן עזאי, a תנא and colleague of רבי עקיבא
Teaches or recites a tradition

phrases.english: Ben Azzai said to him,
this is how Rabbi Yehoshua would teach it:
an additional offering — none at the afternoon prayer,
a wood offering — none at the closing prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ בֶּן עַזַּאי, כָּךְ הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שׁוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's version with a competing tradition from רבי יהושע
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's matching of מוסף with נעילה and קרבן עצים with מנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their teacher's received tradition matched these two items the other way around

steps.title: רבי עקיבא accepts בן עזאי's version
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא changed his teaching to follow בן עזאי's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went back and began teaching like בן עזאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא accepts the correction. From then on he teaches the rule the way בן עזאי reported it from רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the disagreement. The final version is: הלל cancels שחרית, מוסף cancels מנחה, and קרבן עצים cancels נעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Retracted or changed his position

steps.whatToRemember: Final version: הלל means no מעמד at שחרית, מוסף means none at מנחה, and קרבן עצים means none at נעילה. רבי עקיבא adopted בן עזאי's report of רבי יהושע's teaching.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva retracted
to teach in accordance with Ben Azzai.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹנֶה כְּבֶן עַזַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by accepting it
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The accepted version follows רבי יהושע as reported by בן עזאי.

steps.title: The nine dates when families brought wood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts listing the nine dates for the wood offering and the families who brought it. It begins with ראש חודש ניסן and continues through ט״ו באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The times for the wood of the כהנים and the people are nine. On א׳ ניסן: the descendants of ארח בן יהודה. On כ׳ תמוז: the descendants of דוד בן יהודה. On ה׳ אב: the descendants of פרעוש בן יהודה. On ז׳ אב: the descendants of יונדב בן רכב. On י׳ אב: the descendants of סנאה בן בנימין. On ט״ו אב: the descendants of זתוא בן יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains the קרבן עצים it just mentioned. It lists the set dates when particular families donated wood for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these dates was a kind of private יום טוב for that family. The משנה promises nine dates, but only six appear here. The remaining three are listed in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: The set times for wood donated by כהנים and the people
Descendants (of a family line)
Of it, meaning the same month just mentioned (here, אב)

steps.confusionAlert: When the משנה says "בְּשִׁבְעָה בּוֹ", the word "בּוֹ" means the same month, אב. It is not a new month.

phrases.english: The times for the wood of the priests and the people are nine:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן בְּנֵי אָרַח בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: on the first of Nisan, the descendants of Araḥ ben Yehuda;

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֶשְׂרִים בְּתַמּוּז בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: on the twentieth of Tammuz, the descendants of David ben Yehuda;

phrases.aramaic: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה בְּאָב בְּנֵי פַרְעוֹשׁ בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: on the fifth of Av, the descendants of Parosh ben Yehuda;

phrases.aramaic: בְּשִׁבְעָה בּוֹ בְּנֵי יוֹנָדָב בֶּן רֵכָב,
phrases.english: on the seventh of it (Av), the descendants of Jonadab ben Rechab;

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲשָׂרָה בּוֹ בְּנֵי סְנָאָה בֶּן בִּנְיָמִין,
phrases.english: on the tenth of it, the descendants of Sena'a ben Binyamin;

phrases.aramaic: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בּוֹ בְּנֵי זַתּוּא בֶּן יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: on the fifteenth of it, the descendants of Zattu ben Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְמַן עֲצֵי כֹהֲנִים וְהָעָם, תִּשְׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the קרבן עצים mentioned in the previous rule by listing its dates
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are nine fixed dates for family wood donations. The first six are listed here.

steps.title: Who joined the family of Zattu on the fifteenth of Av
steps.stepSummary: On ט״ו באב, the family of זתוא was joined by כהנים, לוים, anyone unsure of his שבט, the בני גונבי עלי, and the בני קוצעי קציעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with them were כהנים and לוים, and anyone who was mistaken about his שבט, and the descendants of the pestle-deceivers, and the descendants of the fig-packers.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that ט״ו באב was a wider day. Several other groups brought wood together with the family of זתוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People who did not know their own family line, or who had no set day of their own, were included on ט״ו באב. The two unusual group names refer to families who used clever tricks to bring wood or ביכורים at a time when it was forbidden. The גמרא explains these names later.

keyTerms.meaning: Who was unsure or mistaken about which שבט he came from
Those who tricked the authorities using a pestle
Those who packed or pressed dried figs

phrases.english: And with them were priests and Levites,
and anyone who erred regarding his tribe,
and the descendants of those who deceived with a pestle
and the descendants of those who packed dried figs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעִמָּהֶם כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the ט״ו באב entry by naming the additional groups who joined the family of זתוא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ט״ו באב, many other groups brought wood together with the family of זתוא.

steps.title: The last three wood-offering dates
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list: בני פחת מואב on כ׳ באב, בני עדין on כ׳ באלול, and בני פרעוש a second time on א׳ בטבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the twentieth of that month (אב), the family of פחת מואב son of יהודה brought the wood. On the twentieth of אלול, the family of עדין son of יהודה. On the first of טבת, the family of פרעוש came back for a second time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of the nine days when families brought wood for the מזבח. These are the last three dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "בעשרים בו" means the twentieth of the month just mentioned, which is אב. בני פרעוש already appeared once earlier in the list, on ה׳ באב, so here the משנה says they came back a second time ("שבו שניה"). That completes all nine dates.

keyTerms.meaning: On the twentieth of it, meaning the twentieth of the same month (אב)
A family descended from יהודה who brought wood on כ׳ באב
A family descended from יהודה who brought wood on כ׳ באלול
Came back a second time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בני פרעוש is a new family. They already brought wood on ה׳ באב, and this is their second turn.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֶשְׂרִים בּוֹ בְּנֵי פַּחַת מוֹאָב בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: On the twentieth of it (Av): the family of Pahat Moav son of Judah;
phrases.notes: "בו" refers back to the month of אב mentioned just before.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֶשְׂרִים בֶּאֱלוּל בְּנֵי עָדִין בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: on the twentieth of Elul: the family of Adin son of Judah;

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בְּטֵבֵת שָׁבוּ בְּנֵי פַרְעוֹשׁ שְׁנִיָּה.
phrases.english: on the first of Tevet the family of Parosh returned a second time.
phrases.notes: Their first turn was on ה׳ באב.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעֶשְׂרִים בּוֹ בְּנֵי פַּחַת מוֹאָב בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of wood-offering dates after ט״ו באב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last three wood-offering dates are כ׳ באב, כ׳ באלול, and א׳ בטבת.

steps.title: No מעמד at all on the first of Tevet
steps.stepSummary: On א׳ בטבת there was no מעמד the entire day, because it had הלל, a קרבן מוסף, and a קרבן עצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first of טבת there was no מעמד at all, because that day had הלל, a קרבן מוסף, and a קרבן עצים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the rule it taught earlier to show a special day when all three cancelling factors come together. On that day the מעמד disappears completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: א׳ בטבת is ראש חודש, so it has a קרבן מוסף, and it falls during חנוכה, so it has הלל. It is also a wood-offering day. Under the rule settled in steps 14–15, each of these factors cancels a different gathering: הלל cancels שחרית, מוסף cancels מנחה, and קרבן עצים cancels נעילה. With all three on one day, the משנה states that there was no מעמד that day.

keyTerms.meaning: The group of local Israelites who gathered to pray and read Torah while their משמר served in the בית המקדש
Psalms of praise, said on ראש חודש and חנוכה
The extra offering brought on special days like ראש חודש
The wood offering, a family's donation of wood for the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: א׳ בטבת is the one day when all three factors combine. The משנה simply states that on that day there was no מעמד, giving these three factors as the reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a real-life example that shows the earlier rule in action. Each factor cancels a different part of the day.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בְּטֵבֵת לֹא הָיָה בּוֹ מַעֲמָד,
phrases.english: On the first of Tevet there was no ma'amad at all,
because it had Hallel
and an additional offering and a wood offering.
phrases.notes: מוסף because it is ראש חודש; עצים because of בני פרעוש.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאֶחָד בְּטֵבֵת לֹא הָיָה בּוֹ מַעֲמָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the cancellation rule from steps 13–15 to the last date listed in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When הלל, מוסף, and קרבן עצים all fall on one day, every מעמד gathering is cancelled.

steps.title: New משנה: five tragedies on two dates
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens: five tragedies happened to our ancestors on שבעה עשר בתמוז and five on תשעה באב. It then begins the list for שבעה עשר בתמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five things happened to our ancestors on the seventeenth of תמוז, and five on the ninth of אב. On the seventeenth of תמוז...
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here: the sad days when we fast. The line ends with "On the seventeenth of תמוז" because the משנה is setting up the list of those five tragedies, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה moves from the happy days of the קרבן עצים to the communal fast days. It first gives a total of five tragedies for each of the two dates. Then it starts to name the events of שבעה עשר בתמוז one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: Five things, meaning five tragedies
Happened to our ancestors
The seventeenth of תמוז, a fast day
The ninth of אב, the major fast day of mourning

phrases.english: Five matters occurred to our forefathers
on the seventeenth of Tammuz,
and five on the Ninth of Av.
On the seventeenth of Tammuz:
phrases.notes: Setup line; the list of tragedies continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים אֵירְעוּ אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּתַמּוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the communal fast days, after the wood-offering section ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five tragedies happened on שבעה עשר בתמוז and five on תשעה באב.
